findings.title: deleteMany OR branch has no method filter and deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. The SMS cron therefore deletes *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeded 1, including rows with future scheduledDate. Today only this handler increments retryCount, but as soon as the email/WhatsApp schedulers (or any other code) reuse the same column, this cron will silently destroy their pending reminders. Add the method filter inside the OR branch (or combine it as `AND` with method/scheduled conditions).

findings.title: prisma.update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unprotected. If this update fails (record removed concurrently, connection error, etc.) the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behaviour where a single failing reminder was only logged. Wrap the retry-count update in its own try/catch (or move it after logging and guard it).

findings.title: retryCount predicate is unindexed, forcing a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron tick
findings.body: `retryCount` has no index (see `WorkflowReminder` indexes in schema.prisma), and because it is an `OR` branch Postgres can no longer satisfy the whole delete from the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index — it must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder. WorkflowReminder is one of the largest tables in this schema and this cron runs frequently, so this adds a repeated full-table scan plus row locks. Either add an index covering retryCount (e.g. `@@index([method, retryCount])`) or fold the retry condition into the existing method/scheduledDate-filtered predicate.

findings.title: retryCount is not incremented when sendTo or message is missing, so those reminders still loop forever
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (else-branch) or in the catch. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. no smsReminderNumber on the booking / no sendTo on the step) or the template produced an empty message, the loop body does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false`, keeps being picked up by the 7-day query on every cron run and is never cleaned up until scheduledDate passes. This is exactly the "keep scheduling it in our cron job until the date is reached" problem the PR claims to fix, so the fix is incomplete for that class of rows.

findings.title: Reminders skipped for non-transient reasons (e.g. SMS sending locked) are permanently deleted
findings.body: `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value not only on send failures but also when sending is suppressed for the user/team (SMS lock state checks inside the provider). With this change such a skip increments `retryCount`, and after two cron runs the reminder row is deleted by the new `deleteMany` branch. Consequence: once a lock/review is lifted the reminder no longer exists and the customer never gets the SMS. Distinguish genuine scheduling errors from intentional skips before counting a retry.

findings.title: Read-modify-write on retryCount instead of atomic increment
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap (cron overlap, manual POST, retried request), both read the same value and one increment is lost, so a reminder can keep retrying beyond the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

findings.title: No test covering the new retry/delete behaviour
findings.body: The PR introduces a retry-and-delete policy (increment on failure, delete when retryCount > 1) with no accompanying test. A regression here either leaks reminders forever or deletes reminders that should still be sent, both of which are silent in production. A unit/integration test asserting (a) retryCount increments when scheduleSMS fails or returns falsy, (b) rows with retryCount > 1 are deleted, and (c) non-SMS reminders are untouched, would lock the behaviour in.
